name: R2-10 candidate causal predictor families and null/trivial baselines (finite, DEV-only-tunable grids)
principle: Families are candidates, not predetermined winners. R2-06 found same-layer transition dependence (median NMI ~0.099, 'measurable but modest') -- this does NOT preselect a Markov/transition predictor as correct; it is one candidate among several, benchmarked on equal footing. Before adding materially more complex ML models, this Phase 0 freezes only causal, deterministic, finite-grid families; whether they are sufficient is an R2-10-DEV-tournament question, not decided here.
common_requirements: explicit causal state (built only from causal_boundary.json.allowed events)
deterministic implementation (no RNG, or RNG explicitly seeded and recorded)

families.name: Trivial/global-frequency baseline
families.causal_state: cumulative count of each expert_id observed in the same-layer stream up to and including position i.
families.role: null/trivial baseline (section 7), not expected to be competitive; establishes the floor.

families.name: Recent-set / last-observation baseline
families.causal_state: the single most recent same-layer expert_set observed at position i (or the empty set at cold start).
families.score_rule: score(e) = 1.0 if e in last_observed_set else 0.0
families.role: null/trivial baseline (section 7); tests whether simple persistence beats global frequency.

families.name: Recency-based predictor (fixed-width sliding window frequency)
families.causal_state: count of each expert_id within the last W same-layer observations ending at position i (ring buffer).

families.name: Transition / Markov-style predictor (order-1, same layer)
families.causal_state: empirical transition counts P(next_expert | current_expert) accumulated causally over same-layer consecutive pairs up to position i, using the SAME token-to-token same-layer transition unit R2-06 already defined (pairwise set-to-set expansion for multi-expert source/target).
families.score_rule: score(e) = sum over experts c in the CURRENT observed set at position i of transition_count[c][e], normalized is not required since only relative order matters for top-k selection.
families.role: candidate family; directly operationalizes the R2-06 same-layer transition-dependence finding as a predictor rather than assuming it transfers.

families.name: Decayed transition/frequency predictor
families.causal_state: same as markov_transition but with exponential decay applied to counts at each new observation, decay_factor < 1 (mirrors R2-09A's aged_frequency caching family, applied here to transition counts instead of residency counts).

families.name: Combination of recency + frequency + transition information
families.causal_state: linear combination of recency_window, global_frequency, and markov_transition scores, each independently causal.
families.score_rule: score(e) = w_r * recency_window_score(e) + w_f * global_frequency_score(e) + w_t * markov_transition_score(e), scores normalized to [0,1] by their own max before blending to make weights meaningful.
families.role: candidate family; the (1,0,0)/(0,1,0)/(0,0,1) grid points are intentionally degenerate re-expressions of recency_window(W=16 default)/global_frequency/markov_transition, giving the blend a built-in sanity check against its own ingredients.

analytical_reference_only.name: Shuffled/non-causal null (analytical reference)
analytical_reference_only.definition: Same-layer expert sequence is shuffled (breaking true temporal order) before computing any descriptive statistic against it, exactly mirroring the shuffled-null convention already used in R2-06/R2-07 (null_baseline.py in both). Used ONLY to show what a predictor could achieve by chance / marginal structure alone, as a descriptive upper-irrelevance check -- it is explicitly NOT a deployable causal policy and MUST NOT be scored with apply_output_contract as if it were a runtime predictor candidate, and MUST NOT appear in selection_rule.json's selection pool.

deferred_to_full_tournament: Only global_frequency and last_observation are implemented in Phase 0 (argine/research2/r2_10/baselines.py), sufficient to exercise causal_walk.py and output_contract.py end-to-end for the leakage/determinism/cardinality tests. recency_window, markov_transition, decayed_transition, and the blend are frozen here as contract (family_id, causal_state, score_rule, finite grid) but their implementations are written in the R2-10 DEV tournament phase, not Phase 0, per the handoff's instruction to stop at Phase 0.
